findings.title: --format invalid-value error message changes shape and fire point
findings.description: Old code declared --format as click.Choice(["human", "json"], case_sensitive=False). Click rejects unknown values at flag-parse time with a consistent error: "Invalid value for '--format': 'X' is not 'human' or 'json'." exiting 2 before any work runs. New code declares --format as click.STRING and defers validation to resolve_and_validate_formatter(), which fires after formatter-packs are loaded and after type-resolution. The error message is now: "unknown formatter 'X'. Available for COMPAT: human, json, junit, sarif". Scripts or CI wrappers that parse stderr for Click's canonical Choice error text will silently stop matching. The exit code remains 2 in both paths, so automated exit-code checks are unaffected.
findings.affected_consumers: scripts that grep/parse stderr for Click Choice error text; error-message regression tests pinned to the old wording

findings.title: --quiet mutex widened from json-only to all non-human: error message text changes for --quiet --format json
findings.description: Old _reject_quiet_plus_json error: "--quiet and --format json are mutually exclusive: one suppresses stdout, the other asks for structured output. Pick one." New reject_quiet_plus_structured error: "--quiet is incompatible with structured output format 'X'. Drop --quiet, or pick --format human." Any CI script that ran --quiet --format json and parsed stderr for the old error text will fail to match. No existing script could have combined --quiet with junit/sarif because those were not valid Choice values before, so the widening to those is purely additive. CHANGELOG documents this change under Changed. Moderate confidence because parsing the exact error text is an uncommon CI pattern.
findings.affected_consumers: CI scripts parsing the --quiet/--format json error message text; testing harnesses with pinned stderr assertions

findings.title: Diagnostic re-exported from protokit.schema creates two canonical import paths for the same class
findings.description: Diagnostic is already publicly exported from protokit.message (via protokit.message.__init__.__all__). It is now also exported from protokit.schema.__init__.__all__, re-imported from protokit.message.model. Both paths resolve to the same class object so isinstance checks and type identity are unaffected. No breakage today; the risk is that a future refactor splitting Diagnostic could silently diverge the two paths.
findings.affected_consumers: none today; future refactors that relocate Diagnostic

findings.title: FormatterContext.target_type None-for-cross-type semantics not reflected in README example
findings.description: FormatterContext documents that target_type is None when old_target_type != new_target_type. The README slack_summary example accesses ctx.target_type or "(unknown type)" without checking old_target_type/new_target_type. A formatter author following only the example will silently produce (unknown type) on cross-type invocations. This is new API with no existing consumers, so no contract is broken today.
findings.affected_consumers: third-party formatter authors following the README example

residual_risks.description: The COMPAT_BISECT and COMPAT_HISTORY JSON formatters import _bisect_report_to_dict and _history_report_to_dict from protokit.schema.cli at call time. These are private single-underscore helpers in a CLI module. If a future refactor of schema/cli.py renames or removes them, the formatter built-ins fail at runtime with ImportError. The legacy JSON serialization logic should be promoted to a stable location in the model or a dedicated serialization module.

BisectReport.commits_walked is always len(commits) (total range length), including in early-exit paths where fewer commits were actually evaluated. This matches old behavior exactly. Downstream SARIF/JUnit consumers treating commits_walked as "commits evaluated" rather than "commits in range" could misinterpret early-exit results.

testing_gaps.description: No test pins the stderr text and exit code when an unknown --format value is supplied. The old Click Choice validation was exercised implicitly by Click. The new runtime validation in resolve_and_validate_formatter needs explicit tests asserting exit code 2 and the "unknown formatter" error message text for each subcommand kind.

The widened --quiet mutex needs a test asserting that --quiet --format junit exits 2 on protokit diff. The message CLI previously had no quiet+format rejection at all (no _reject_quiet_plus_json equivalent in message/cli.py), so --quiet --format junit on protokit diff is a new rejection requiring a test.

No test covers a cross-type FormatterContext (where target_type is None and old_target_type/new_target_type are set) being passed to a custom formatter, to verify the documented semantics are honored end-to-end.
